about.title: Personal Injury Help in Madera, California
about.longDescription: Madera sits along corridors like Rt 145, Cleveland Avenue W, Tozer Street, and Cleveland Avenue, where public records show a steady share of the city's reported collisions. If you or someone you love was hurt on these roads, at work, or somewhere else in town, LawProactive can help. We're a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and we don't charge you anything to make the connection. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. Getting hurt already brings enough stress; figuring out who to call shouldn't add to it. We simply help you find someone qualified to look at your situation and explain your options, so you can focus on healing while decisions about your claim get the attention they deserve.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the chance to recover anything.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Your Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so your compensation isn't limited by an arbitrary ceiling.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Win
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you don't pay unless there's a recovery. That means getting connected costs you nothing upfront.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Madera?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file most personal injury claims. If your claim involves a government entity, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's wise to act promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my accident?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated entirely.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm ourselves. We simply help connect injured people with an independent attorney who may be able to assist.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Madera?
items.answer: Public records show higher collision counts along corridors such as Rt 145, Cleveland Avenue W, Tozer Street, and Cleveland Avenue, with crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral, publicly reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront if I'm connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if there's a recovery in your case. There's no upfront cost to you for the connection or for the attorney's services unless your case succeeds.
